# 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship: A Comprehensive Report
## 1\. Executive Summary
The **2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship** served as the premier event of the World Seniors Tour (WST) for the 2024/25 season. Held between **May 7 and May 11, 2025**, at the **Crucible Theatre** in Sheffield, England, the tournament marked the 16th staging of the championship. As the crown jewel of the seniors circuit, the event followed immediately after the professional World Snooker Championship, maintaining the city’s status as the global epicenter of the sport during May.

The tournament was won by the English qualifier **Alfie Burden**, who defeated the 2018 champion **Aaron Canavan** of Jersey by **8 frames to 4** in the final. Burden's victory was a defining moment in a tumultuous year for the Londoner, who had been relegated from the professional circuit only weeks prior. His triumph at the Crucible—after losing the final in 2023—provided a narrative of redemption and resilience that would propel him to further success later in the calendar year.

Beyond the competitive outcomes, the 2025 Championship was a watershed moment for the sport’s officiating history. It served as the final professional engagement for **Michaela Tabb**, the pioneering referee who became the first woman to officiate a World Championship final. Tabb presided over the opening session of the final before formally retiring from the traditional form of the game, handing over her duties in an emotional farewell ceremony.

This report provides an exhaustive analysis of the tournament, detailing the qualification pathways, the operational context, the match-by-match progression, the commercial landscape, and the broader legacy of the event within the annals of snooker history.

## 2\. Tournament Infrastructure and Context
### 2.1 The World Seniors Tour Ecosystem
The World Seniors Championship is not an isolated event but the culmination of a global season organized by World Seniors Snooker (WSS). By 2025, the tour had matured into a robust secondary circuit designed to honor the legends of the game while providing high-level competition for amateurs aged over 40 and professionals aged over 45 (ranked outside the top 64).

The 2024/25 season operated under a "Race to the Crucible" format. Players accumulated ranking points across a series of qualifying events held internationally, with the highest-ranked competitors earning coveted spots in the final stages at Sheffield. This meritocratic system ensured that the field was not merely a collection of exhibition players but included battle-hardened match players currently active on the amateur and secondary professional circuits.

Key qualification pathways included:

* **Continental Championships:** Winners of the European, Pan-American, African, and Asia-Pacific Seniors Championships received direct entry, ensuring global representation. 
* **Golden Ticket Events:** Specific qualifying tournaments held in the UK offered direct spots to the winners. 
* **Invited Legends:** To ensure commercial viability and fan engagement, wildcard invitations were extended to icons of the sport such as Jimmy White, Ken Doherty, and Tony Knowles.

### 2.2 Host Venue: The Crucible Theatre
For the seventh consecutive year, the championship was staged at the **Crucible Theatre**. The venue, synonymous with snooker since 1977, provides a unique "pressure cooker" atmosphere due to its intimate 980-seat configuration.

The 2025 event was held against the backdrop of a significant administrative victory for the tour. Just prior to the tournament, it was announced that the World Seniors Championship would remain at the Crucible until at least **2027**. This extension was part of a strategic partnership between World Seniors Snooker and **Sheffield City Council**, designed to leverage the city's snooker heritage for economic and community benefit.

#### 2.2.1 Community Integration: The "Seniors of Sheffield"
In 2025, the tournament expanded its footprint beyond the baize. The organizers introduced **"Sheffield Youth and Business Days"** alongside the established **"Sheffield Seniors Day."** These initiatives involved collaboration with **Sheffield Hallam University**, where sports business management students were integrated into the event's operational and broadcast delivery teams. This symbiotic relationship transformed the tournament from a mere sporting contest into a vehicle for educational development and local business networking.

### 2.3 Broadcast and Media Production
In the United Kingdom, the tournament was broadcast exclusively on terrestrial television via **Channel 5**. The network, which had broadcast the event since 2023, renewed its commitment to the seniors tour, ensuring that the matches were available to a mass audience rather than being paywalled.

The production was handled by **Sunset+Vine**, a heavyweight in sports broadcasting. The production quality mirrored that of the main professional tour, utilizing a multi-camera setup, distinct graphics packages, and a roving floor reporter. The commentary booth featured voices deeply embedded in snooker's history, including:

* **Dennis Taylor:** 1985 World Champion. 
* **John Virgo:** Former UK Champion and veteran commentator. 
* **Cliff Thorburn:** The 1980 World Champion.

This continuity of talent provided a nostalgic auditory backdrop that resonated with the demographic of the viewing audience. Internationally, the event was distributed through a network of partners, including streaming services in China and digital platforms in Europe, reflecting the global participation base.

### 2.4 Prize Fund and Sponsorship
The title sponsorship was held by **JenningsBet**, continuing a multi-year association with the World Seniors Tour.

**Prize Money Distribution:**

* **Winner:** £20,000 
* **Runner-up:** £10,000 
* **Semi-Finalists:** £5,000 (estimated based on tour structures)

While the prize fund is modest compared to the multi-million pound purses of the main tour, the prestige of the title remains the primary motivator. However, the commercial portfolio for 2025 included a high-value "traditional" bonus.

The Maximum Break Prize: 
In a nod to the sport's golden era of the 1980s and 90s, where 147 breaks were often rewarded with luxury vehicles, the local automotive partner BYD Lookers Sheffield offered a BYD SEAL U electric SUV to any player compiling a maximum break during the championship. The vehicle was displayed prominently outside the Crucible Theatre throughout the week, serving as a major fan attraction and talking point, although the prize ultimately went unclaimed.

## 3\. The Field: Profiles and Qualifiers
The 2025 field consisted of 16 players, representing a diverse mix of former world champions and current amateur standouts.

### 3.1 The "Legends" (Invited & seeded)
* **Jimmy White (England):** The "Whirlwind" entered the tournament as a four-time World Seniors Champion. Despite his age, White remained the tour's biggest draw, having defeated Alfie Burden in the 2023 final. His form on the main tour had declined, but his affinity for the seniors format made him a perennial favorite. 
* **Ken Doherty (Ireland):** The 1997 World Professional Champion and 2024 Seniors runner-up. Doherty combined his media duties with a competitive game that relied on tactical astuteness. 
* **Joe Perry (England):** A recent addition to the seniors ranks, Perry was still competing at a high level professionally shortly before the event. His presence as a "young" senior (aged just over 50\) made him the pre-tournament bookmakers' favorite. 
* **Tony Drago (Malta):** The "Tornado" remains one of the fastest players in history. His inclusion guaranteed entertainment, and his recent form on the seniors circuit suggested he was a genuine contender. 
* **Dominic Dale (Wales):** The eccentric "Spaceman," a double ranking event winner on the main tour. Dale's heavy scoring power was considered his greatest asset in the shorter seniors formats.

### 3.2 The Qualifiers (The "Race to the Crucible" Winners)
* **Igor Figueiredo (Brazil):** The Defending Champion. Figueiredo had won the 2024 title and the Pan-American championship. He carried the hopes of South America but faced the pressure of retaining his crown. 
* **Alfie Burden (England):** Qualifying via the tour rankings/qualifiers after falling off the main tour. Burden was driven by the "pain" of his 2023 final defeat and his recent relegation. 
* **Aaron Canavan (Jersey):** The 2018 World Seniors Champion. Canavan, an amateur from Jersey, had proven his ability to handle the Crucible pressure seven years prior. 
* **Hassan Kerde (Australia):** The Asia-Pacific Champion. Kerde's qualification highlighted the tour's expansion into Oceania. 
* **Charl Jonck (South Africa):** The African Champion. Jonck is the dominant force in African snooker, regularly representing the continent at world events. 
* **Wayne Townsend (England):** A dangerous amateur qualifier known for his giant-killing abilities in the UK club scene. 
* **Craig Steadman (England):** The reigning European Seniors Champion. A former pro with a smooth technique. 
* **Gerard Greene (Northern Ireland):** Greene arrived in Sheffield on the back of an incredible **15-match winning streak** on the World Seniors Tour, making him the form player of the qualifiers.

## 4\. Tournament Narrative: Round by Round Analysis
### 4.1 Round 1 (Last 16\) – Wednesday May 7 & Thursday May 8
The opening round was characterized by the immediate exit of the defending champion and the collision of two titans in the draw.

The Shock of the Round: Exit of the Champion 
Defending champion Igor Figueiredo opened his campaign against English qualifier Wayne Townsend. Despite Figueiredo's pedigree and his victory in 2024, he appeared unsettled by the occasion. Townsend, playing with freedom, capitalized on the Brazilian's errors. The match, a best-of-7 encounter, saw Townsend secure a 4–2 victory, blowing the top half of the draw wide open immediately. 
The Grudge Match: Burden vs. White 
The draw threw up a rematch of the 2023 final in the very first round: Alfie Burden vs. Jimmy White. While White had the crowd's support, Burden had the superior form. The match was one-sided, with Burden dominating the tactical exchanges and scoring heavily when chances arose. He ran out a 4–1 winner, a result that signaled his intent to the rest of the field. This victory was psychologically pivotal for Burden, exorcising the demons of his previous final defeat to the same opponent. 
The Thriller: Drago vs. Greene 
The match between Tony Drago and Gerard Greene was the highlight of the first round in terms of drama. Greene, riding his 15-match winning streak, looked set to extend it. However, Drago produced a performance of extraordinary grit.

* *Key Moments:* In both the second and third frames, the scores were tied after the final black was potted, necessitating a **re-spotted black**. Remarkably, Drago won *both* of these high-pressure tie-breakers. 
* *Outcome:* Despite Greene's form, the "Tornado" held his nerve in the deciding frame to win **4–3**. This match demonstrated that while Drago's speed is legendary, his match-play temperament remains elite.

**Other Key Results:**

* **Dominic Dale** displayed his scoring threat early, dispatching European Champion **Craig Steadman** **4–2**. 
* **Joe Perry** avoided an upset against Brazilian qualifier **Fabio Anderson Luersen**, winning **4–2** to justify his favorite status. 
* **Aaron Canavan** proved too strong for **Andrew Norman**, winning **4–1**. 
* **Hassan Kerde** announced himself with a **4–0** whitewash of 1980s icon **Tony Knowles**, while South Africa's **Charl Jonck** scored a significant upset by beating **Ken Doherty** **4–2**, ending the Irishman's hopes of a second final in three years.

### 4.2 Quarter-Finals – Friday May 9
As the tournament reached the quarter-final stage, the pressure of the single-table setup began to mount.

The Comeback: Burden vs. Drago 
The quarter-final between Alfie Burden and Tony Drago is destined to be remembered as a classic of the seniors genre. Drago started ferociously, punishing a sluggish Burden to race into a 3–0 lead. In a race to four, Burden was on the brink of elimination. 
However, the intermission shifted the momentum. Burden returned with a renewed focus, tightening his safety game to deny Drago the open reds he craves. Frame by frame, the Londoner clawed back the deficit. Drago, visibly frustrated as his rhythm was disrupted, could not halt the slide. Burden won four consecutive frames to steal the match 4–3, a victory from the jaws of defeat that often characterizes eventual champions. 
Dale's Masterclass 
Dominic Dale faced the favorite Joe Perry in a match that many expected to be the de facto final. Instead, it was a procession. Dale's scoring was relentless, and he punished every safety error from Perry. The 4–1 scoreline was a comprehensive statement, installing Dale as the new favorite in the eyes of many pundits. 
Global Representation 
In the other quarter-finals, Hassan Kerde continued his dream run by defeating Charl Jonck. This guaranteed an Australian representative in the semi-finals. Meanwhile, Aaron Canavan ended the run of giant-killer Wayne Townsend, proving that his 2018 title was a foundation for consistent performance at this level.

### 4.3 Semi-Finals – Saturday May 10
The semi-finals produced a contrast in styles: one match a blowout, the other a high-scoring tug-of-war.

Semi-Final 1: Alfie Burden vs. Hassan Kerde 
Burden carried the momentum from his quarter-final escape directly into this match. He started with lethal precision, compiling breaks of 57 and 65 to race into a 4–0 lead. Kerde, appearing in his first Crucible semi-final, struggled to settle under the TV lights. 
Although the Australian rallied to win two frames and reduce the deficit to 4–2, Burden extinguished any hopes of a comeback with a decisive break of 97 in the seventh frame.

* **Result:** **Alfie Burden 5–2 Hassan Kerde** (Score inferred from "secured his place by taking the next frame" after 4-2 ).

Semi-Final 2: Dominic Dale vs. Aaron Canavan 
This match was defined by the clash between Dale's break-building ceiling and Canavan's match-winning floor. The early frames were shared 2–2. Then, Dale unleashed the heaviest scoring of the tournament:

* Frame 5: **109** clearance. 
* Frame 6: 131 total clearance (The highest break of the tournament). 
 Despite conceding back-to-back centuries, Canavan did not buckle. He utilized his tactical experience to drag Dale into scrappier frames where the Welshman's fluency was nullified. In a display of immense mental fortitude, Canavan won the final three frames to upset the form player of the week. 
* **Result:** **Aaron Canavan 5–4 Dominic Dale**.

## 5\. The Final: Burden vs. Canavan
Date: Sunday, May 11, 2025 
Venue: Crucible Theatre, Sheffield 
Format: Best of 15 Frames (Played over 3 sessions) 
Referees: Michaela Tabb (Session 1), Proletina Velichkova (Sessions 2 & 3\)

### 5.1 The Narrative Arc
For Alfie Burden, this was a career-defining moment. A professional since 1994, he had never won a ranking event (at this point in time). His relegation from the main tour in April 2025 had left him at a crossroads. Victory would validate his decision to continue playing; defeat would be a second seniors final loss in three years. 
For Aaron Canavan, victory would make him only the second player (after Jimmy White) to win multiple World Seniors titles, cementing his legacy as the greatest amateur senior player of his generation.

### 5.2 Session 1: Tabb's Farewell and Burden's Start
The match began with high emotion as Michaela Tabb walked out to officiate her final frames. The crowd afforded her a prolonged ovation. 
Canavan settled quickest, taking the opening frame 66–48. However, Burden responded immediately. Playing with an aggression that belied the stakes, he reeled off four consecutive frames. His safety play forced Canavan into difficult openings, which Burden ruthlessly exploited.

* **End of Session 1:** **Alfie Burden 4–1 Aaron Canavan** 
* *Ceremony:* At the conclusion of the fifth frame, play was paused. Michaela Tabb formally handed her white gloves to Proletina Velichkova, marking the end of her 24-year career as a referee of professional snooker.

### 5.3 Session 2: The Century and the Surge
Resuming with a three-frame advantage, Burden did not let up. He extended his lead to 5–1, and then 6–2 (trading frames). 
In the eighth frame, Burden produced the highlight of the final: a magnificent break of 109\. This was the only century of the final and demonstrated that Burden was playing at a standard far above the amateur level. 
At 7–2, Burden was one frame from victory. However, the "Crucible line" is notoriously hard to cross. Canavan, showing the resilience that beat Dale, dug deep to win the final frame of the session (78–32) and the first of the evening to close the gap.

* **Score at Intermission:** **Alfie Burden 7–3 Aaron Canavan** (approximate based on flow).

### 5.4 Session 3: The Crowning Moment
Canavan continued to fight, but the deficit was too large. In the 12th frame, Burden constructed a match-winning contribution. As the final balls were potted, the relief on his face was palpable.

* **Final Score:** **Alfie Burden 8–4 Aaron Canavan**.

### 5.5 Post-Match Reaction
In his victory interview, Burden was visibly emotional. "It's been a massive journey with so many ups and downs," he told the studio team. "I think I've underachieved in my career but you've got to enjoy this moment". 
He dedicated the win to his family and the support system that kept him playing after losing his tour card. The victory earned him £20,000 and the World Seniors trophy.

## 6\. Statistical Analysis
### 6.1 Century Breaks
The 2025 Championship saw a total of five century breaks, a high number for the seniors format, indicating the quality of the playing conditions and the standard of the field.

Dominic Dale's four centuries in a single tournament is a modern seniors record, highlighting his dominance in the scoring department despite his semi-final exit.

### 6.2 Prize Money Breakdown
## 7\. Broader Impact and Legacy
### 7.1 The "Burden Boost"
Alfie Burden's victory at the 2025 World Seniors Championship had immediate and profound consequences for his career. The confidence gained from lifting a world title at the Crucible acted as a catalyst. Remarkably, later in December 2025, Burden—competing as an amateur top-up in the Snooker Shoot Out (a professional ranking event)—went on to win the tournament. 
This made Burden the oldest first-time winner of a ranking event in history (at age 49\) and validated the Seniors Tour as a genuine pathway for players to regain professional form. His trajectory from relegation to Seniors Champion to Ranking Event Winner in a single calendar year is unique in the sport's history.

### 7.2 The Future of the Championship
The 2025 event was a commercial success, prompting immediate expansion plans. World Seniors Snooker announced that the **2026 World Seniors Championship** would expand its field to **24 players**, utilizing a two-table setup for the early rounds to accommodate the extra matches. This expansion reflects the growing demand from international federations to send representatives to Sheffield.

Furthermore, the broadcasting landscape for the seniors game was solidified with the announcement that Channel 5 would broadcast the new **British Seniors Open** in Derby later in 2025, creating a multi-event televised calendar for the first time in years.

### 7.3 The End of an Era for Officiating
The retirement of Michaela Tabb marked the severance of one of the last links to the early 2000s boom of snooker. Her departure was handled with the dignity befitting her status, and her endorsement of the new generation of female referees, specifically naming **Desislava Bozhilova**, ensured a passing of the torch that was celebrated by the global snooker community.

## 8\. Conclusion
The 2025 World Seniors Championship will be remembered as a tournament of redemption. For Alfie Burden, it was the start of a fairytale resurgence. For the World Seniors Tour, it was a confirmation of its growing stature, evidenced by the expansion plans and the retention of the Crucible contract. And for the fans, it was a final chance to salute a pioneering official. As the snooker world looked toward the 2025/26 season, the seniors circuit had firmly established itself not as a graveyard for elephants, but as a vibrant theatre of dreams where careers could be reborn.

Alfie Burden Wins 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship
=====================================================================

12th May 2025

[Home](https://wpbsa.com/) » Alfie Burden Wins 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship

**Alfie Burden is the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker champion after he defeated Aaron Canavan 8-4 at the Crucible Theatre on Sunday.**

*   [Results](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/results)

The 48-year-old, who was the last player to qualify for the event via the Golden Ticket Play-Off last month, came through a strong field at the sport’s most famous venue to lift the most prestigious title in seniors snooker for the first time.

![Image 10: A man in black suit raises a trophy above his head in front of crowd](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_2336-300x200.jpg)

Burden’s campaign began with a repeat of the 2023 World Seniors Snooker Championship final and he exacted revenge on four-time winner Jimmy White, before showing his fighting qualities from 3-0 down against Maltese legend Tony Drago to advance to the semi-finals.

A comfortable 6-2 victory over Australian debutant Hassan Kerde then set up a title match meeting with 2018 champion Aaron Canavan from Jersey after he stunned Dominic Dale in the last four.

![Image 11: Two men in suits standing on either side of a woman in a suit, all three in front of a snooker table with balls on it and a trophy](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0003-300x200.jpg)

The best-of-15 frame final was split into three mini-sessions of five frames and the first of these saw a moment of history as Michaela Tabb, who became the first female referee to take charge of a World Snooker Championship final in 2009, took charge of her final frames at the Crucible Theatre.

It was Canavan who broke the deadlock but the Englishman quickly hit back to take four successive frames, with help from contributions of 74 and 54, to lead 4-1 at the first break.

![Image 12: A snooker player in a black suit leans over a green snooker table, aiming to hit the cue ball, with an audience in the background](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0086-300x200.jpg)

A 75 saw the cueist from Jersey reduce the deficit before Burden once again showed off his scoring prowess by hit consecutive breaks 65, 109 and 80 to move one away from victory at 7-2.

Canavan was able to avoid defeat before the second interval as he took frame 10 and further threatened a comeback by taking the next to put the scoreline at 7-4.

![Image 13: A man playing snooker with an audience in the background](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0029-300x200.jpg)

Burden admitted afterwards that, even at 7-3 ahead, he had told his coach Patsy Fagan that he “wasn’t fancying winning” but there were few signs of nerves in the title-winning frame as he fired in a flamboyant break of 76 to get over the line as an 8-4 victor.

![Image 14: Snooker player Mark Allen poses with a trophy and two people, in front of an audience and a snooker table](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_2318-300x200.jpg)

Following the victory, Burden said: “I’m absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It’s been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it’s been well documented that I think I’ve underachieved in my career but you’ve got to enjoy this moment.

“It was a strong field this week and I felt like I played the best snooker and deserved to win the tournament. Jimmy White texted me this morning and so did Ken Doherty – we are all great friends and players get behind each other. Only one person can win and this was my week.”

![Image 15: Ken Doherty kisses the trophy in a snooker competition while a woman in the background applauds](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0362-300x200.jpg)

Alfie Burden claims World Seniors Snooker Championship crown
============================================================

by [David Caulfield](https://snookerhq.com/author/snookerhq/ "Posts by David Caulfield")on May 12, 2025

*   ![Image 6: A man with short brown hair is wearing a black shirt and looking at the camera](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/c2e07db741a2d9d83099370357cb654b720cd070580680bead2ec17cf41652f3?s=85&d=mm&r=g)[David Caulfield](https://snookerhq.com/author/snookerhq/ "Posts by David Caulfield")Author

### More in Finals:

*   [![Image 8: Alfie Burden wins the 2025 Snooker Shoot Out](blob:http://localhost/bc6b234ccea4a4101c5e098d1bbe8bea)](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/14/from-relegation-to-ranking-winner-alfie-burden-incredible-shoot-out-story/ "Permalink to From relegation to ranking winner: Alfie Burden’s incredible Shoot Out story")[From relegation to ranking winner: Alfie Burden’s incredible Shoot Out story](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/14/from-relegation-to-ranking-winner-alfie-burden-incredible-shoot-out-story/ "Permalink to From relegation to ranking winner: Alfie Burden’s incredible Shoot Out story")December 14, 2025
*   [![Image 10: Alfie Burden wins the 2025 Snooker Shoot Out](blob:http://localhost/bc6b234ccea4a4101c5e098d1bbe8bea)](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/10/jamie-clarke-at-the-double-on-snookers-q-tour/ "Permalink to Jamie Clarke strikes double with another Q Tour title")[Jamie Clarke strikes double with another Q Tour title](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/10/jamie-clarke-at-the-double-on-snookers-q-tour/ "Permalink to Jamie Clarke strikes double with another Q Tour title")December 10, 2025
*   [![Image 12: Alfie Burden wins the 2025 Snooker Shoot Out](blob:http://localhost/bc6b234ccea4a4101c5e098d1bbe8bea)](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/08/extra-special-reactions-as-mark-selby-seals-10th-triple-crown-title-with-uk-win/ "Permalink to ‘Extra special’: reactions as Mark Selby seals 10th Triple Crown title with UK win")[‘Extra special’: reactions as Mark Selby seals 10th Triple Crown title with UK win](https://snookerhq.com/2025/12/08/extra-special-reactions-as-mark-selby-seals-10th-triple-crown-title-with-uk-win/ "Permalink to ‘Extra special’: reactions as Mark Selby seals 10th Triple Crown title with UK win")December 8, 2025

**Alfie Burden won the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship title on Sunday with an 8-4 victory over Aaron Canavan in the final.**

Both players were contesting the title-deciding affair at the World Seniors Snooker Tour’s most prestigious event for the second time.

Canavan was attempting to add a second world crown to the seniors title he [captured back in 2018](https://snookerhq.com/2018/03/25/aaron-canavan-becomes-world-seniors-champion/).

Burden, on the other hand, was bidding to etch his name onto the silverware for the first time having narrowly missed out on glory with defeat in the 2023 final.

Two years ago, Burden was pipped in a close final by Jimmy White, but the Londoner comprehensively overcame the four-time champion in the first round this year.

A 4-1 triumph against White set Burden up to mount a serious challenge again, and his chances increased on the back of a dramatic quarter-final defeat of Tony Drago.

Trailing 3-0 to the Tornado, Burden conjured a remarkable fight back by winning the concluding four frames for a deciding-frame success.

Burden’s 6-2 victory over fellow qualifier Hassan Kerde subsequently saw him reach Sunday’s showdown for the title in Sheffield.

The 48 year-old, who was relegated from the World Snooker Tour at the end of the 2024/25 snooker season after failing to break into the top 64, dominated the final.

After losing the opening frame, he established a 4-1 lead at the mid-session interval and then extended his advantage to 7-2 with breaks of 109 and 81.

When Canavan won two frames on the bounce to reduce his arrears, a repeat of his semi-final heroics seemed to be on the cards.

The Jersey potter won the last four frames to overturn a 5-2 deficit against Dominic Dale and reach the final on Saturday.

But any aspirations of another unlikely turnaround were quashed in the 12th frame when Burden completed the win.

![Image 14: Crucible Theatre](blob:http://localhost/bc6b1d4ba2d7f6b6fd42107ed5f5c56d)

There were big crowds at the Crucible Theatre during the weekend. Photo credit: [Monique Limbos](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/11/the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-sfs/)

“It sounds amazing,” Alfie Burden told [Alisha Singh for the WSST](https://x.com/WorldSeniors/status/1921623376847602153) when asked how it sounded to be the world seniors snooker champion.

“I’m absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It was a bit twitchy at the end.”

“I needed a big bit of luck to get the opportunity, and then I took the opportunity.

“You have enough bad luck in your career, so when a little bit of good fortune comes along, you’ve got to take it with both hands – and I did.

“It’s been a massive journey. There are so many ups and downs being a snooker player.

“I’ve been well documented with saying I’m not happy with how I’ve underachieved in my career.

“But you’ve got to enjoy this moment. We all know I’m not the best over-45 player in the world.

“There are players ineligible to play in this event, but you can only beat what’s in front of you.

“I’ve beaten the best that was on offer. It was a strong field this week. I felt like I played the best snooker and deserved to win the tournament.”

Victory in the World Seniors Snooker Championship will represent one of the biggest wins in Burden’s career.

He won the 2009 IBSF World Amateur Championship and spent the best part of three decades competing on the World Snooker Tour as a professional.

Burden, who won £20,000 for his exploits at the Crucible Theatre, previously reached a career-high ranking of number 38 in the world.

Jubilant Burden Wins First Ranking Title at Shoot Out
=====================================================

14th December 2025

[Home](https://wpbsa.com/) » Jubilant Burden Wins First Ranking Title at Shoot Out

**Alfie Burden didn’t even know he had a place in the 9Club Shoot Out on the day the tournament started, but he ended up with the trophy, beating Stuart Bingham in the final to land his first ranking title, 30 years after first turning pro.**

_**Tickets for the 2026 Shoot Out in Blackpool are on sale now – for details[CLICK HERE](https://www.wst.tv/shoot-out-2026-tickets)**_

Burden was relegated from the pro tour at the end of last season and, having finished 20th on the Q School ‘top-up’ list did not expect to be offered a place in the unique one-frame knockout tournament. He was about to jump into a swimming pool on Wednesday morning at 9.30am when he had a call from WST’s Bristol office to tell him that Alex Clenshaw had pulled out, and there was a spot in the draw for him if he could drive from London to Blackpool in time for the afternoon session.

He was at the venue within five hours and went on to win seven matches to capture the biggest title of a career which started in 1994. Burden, who turns 49 on Sunday, also won the World Seniors title earlier this year, but tonight’s triumph is by far the biggest moment of his life in snooker.

The former world number 38 had never previously been beyond the quarter-finals of a ranking event but now becomes the only amateur to win a ranking title other than Zhao Xintong who was crowned World Champion this year. The £50,000 top prize is by far the biggest of his career and could be enough to regain his place on tour next season via the one-year ranking list. The tenth different winner in ten ranking events so far this season, he is also in line for a place in next year’s Champion of Champions.

Former World Champion Bingham, seeking his first title since lifting the Masters trophy in 2020, had first chance in the final but made just 6 before missing a mid range red. Burden opened up the pack immediately and went on to make an excellent break of 56. Bingham had one more opportunity to counter but potted just one red before missing a long blue and the handshake soon followed, before Burden jumped on to the table to celebrate.

“I can’t believe I have won it,” said Burden, who was a promising footballer for Arsenal in his junior days before switching to snooker after a serious knee injury. “On Wednesday morning I went for a swim and I only had my phone with me because I have lost my locker key at the gym. I was walking out to the swimming pool and I looked at my phone and saw I had a missed call. I rang back and found out I had a place in the Shoot Out. I got changed, dashed to the snooker club to get my cue, dashed home to get my trousers and shoes, then I was on the M1.

“From the start I have played well. Everything fell into place for me. I am a ranking event winner now and that is something I am very proud of. After dropping off the tour last season I found myself in the wilderness. I have had no motivation to play on the Q Tour, I turned up for a few events in terrible shape having not practised. Then a couple of weeks ago I went to the one in Bulgaria with a new cue and got to the semi-finals. Now I am hoping this win will get me back on the tour.

“I was a pro for a long time, I first joined the tour when I was 17. I still have a lot to offer snooker, I am hungry, I love the game and I have people who believe in me. I have a great family and friends, a great mentor in Patsy Fagan. It has been a difficult career, I am not going to lie. Snooker is a very tough sport mentally. There have been a lot more downs than ups, but this is a moment I will cherish. I can’t wait to see my children tomorrow, they have always supported me – this is for them.”

Earlier in the semi-finals, Bingham edged out Iulian Boiko in an exciting finish. Ukraine’s Boiko, enjoying his best run in a ranking event, trailed 44-35 with 40 seconds to go when he missed the pink to a centre pocket, needing just three pots for victory. Burden beat Thailand’s Noppon Saengkham with a break of 73.

World Seniors Snooker Launches New Season with Increased Prize Money
====================================================================

14th July 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » World Seniors Snooker Launches New Season with Increased Prize Money

**World Seniors Snooker (WSS) have today announced the dates for the 2025/26 season which will see nine tour events, with a minimum of four places available for players in their 2026 World Seniors Snooker Championship via the ranking list qualification system**

Changes for the new campaign mean anyone over 40, including World Snooker Tour (WST) professionals, are now eligible to participate in the tour events which will see the winner’s prize doubled each weekend to £1,000 and prize money being paid down to the last 16.

Jason Francis, Chairman of WSS, said “This season there are a lot more players eligible to play, including a number of WST professionals, and we have pledged £27,000 in prize money across our nine events which is more than double the amount that was on offer last season. If you are over 40, now is the time to dust off your cue and come and enjoy some friendly but serious competition”

The season will begin on Friday 15 August 2025 with all events played at the Crucible Sports and Social Club in Reading.

![Image 5: A wide angle view of a snooker match in progress](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_9833-300x200.jpg)

TOUR DATES
----------

### 2025

*   August 15-17
*   September 26-28
*   October 10-12
*   November 21-23
*   December 12-14

### 2026

*   January 16-18
*   February 6-8
*   March 6-8
*   April 3-5

On the Sunday of each weekend, a Super Seniors event will be staged for those aged over 55.

All events are now open for entry via [WPBSA SnookerScores](https://snookerscores.net/organisation/world-seniors-snooker/tournaments). A [WSS Tour membership](https://snookerscores.net/organisation/world-seniors-snooker/memberships) will be required in order to compete in the Race to the Crucible series.

The **2025 World Seniors Championship** (officially the **2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship**) was a [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England, the seventh consecutive year that the tournament was held at the venue. Open to amateur players over 40 and professional players who were over 45 and also ranked outside the top 64 in the [snooker world rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings "Snooker world rankings"), the event was the 16th edition of the [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship"), first held in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Seniors_Championship "1991 World Seniors Championship"). Organised by the [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour"), the event was broadcast in the United Kingdom by [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_(British_TV_channel) "5 (British TV channel)") and internationally by other broadcasters.

[Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") was the defending champion, having defeated [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") 5‍–‍2 in the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Seniors_Championship "2024 World Seniors Championship") final, but he lost 2‍–‍4 to Wayne Townsend in the first round. [Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") held leads of 4‍–‍1 and 7‍–‍2 against [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") in the final and went on to win 8‍–‍4 to claim his first World Seniors title.

The tournament produced five [century breaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break"), four of which were compiled by [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale"), who also made the highest, a 131 in his semi-final match against Canavan. The final of the event was [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb")'s last appearance as a traditional snooker referee, following a 24-year career during which she had refereed two [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") finals.

[![Image 6: The Crucible Theatre from outside](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/52/Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png/330px-Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sheffield_Crucible_theatre.png)

For the seventh consecutive year, the main stage of the tournament was held at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England.

The 2025 World Seniors Championship was a [snooker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker "Snooker") tournament that took place from 7 to 11 May 2025 at the [Crucible Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crucible_Theatre "Crucible Theatre") in [Sheffield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheffield "Sheffield"), England.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) The 16th edition of the [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship"), first played in [1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991_World_Seniors_Championship "1991 World Seniors Championship"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-3) it was held at the Crucible for the seventh consecutive year[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-12) and sponsored by bookmaker JenningsBet.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1) A [World Seniors Tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Tour "World Seniors Tour") event, the tournament was open to amateur players over 40 and professional players over 45, who also needed to be ranked outside the top 64 in the [snooker world rankings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snooker_world_rankings "Snooker world rankings").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-13) The event was broadcast in the United Kingdom on [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_(British_TV_channel) "5 (British TV channel)") and by other broadcasters internationally.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo") was the defending champion, having defeated [Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") 5‍–‍2 in the [2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_World_Seniors_Championship "2024 World Seniors Championship") final.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2024-14) Four referees officiated: Mark Beale, [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb"), Rod Eaton, and Proletina Velichkova.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-15)

Figueiredo, as the defending champion,[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2024-14) and was given the top [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seeding_(sports) "Seeding (sports)").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16) Other seeded players were Doherty, four-time winner of the event [Jimmy White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White"), [Tony Drago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") and [Tony Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Knowles_(snooker_player) "Tony Knowles (snooker player)"). [Joe Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Perry_(snooker_player) "Joe Perry (snooker player)") and [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") retired as professional players after their defeats in the qualifying stages of the [2025 World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Snooker_Championship "2025 World Snooker Championship"), making them eligible to compete. Several players had to qualify. The winner of the [2018 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Seniors_Championship "2018 World Seniors Championship"), [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan"), as well as [Andrew Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Norman_(snooker_player) "Andrew Norman (snooker player)"), [Gerard Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Greene "Gerard Greene") and Townsend, qualified for the event during the so-called Race to the Crucible Series. Four more players qualified through various continental Seniors Championships: [Craig Steadman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Steadman "Craig Steadman") won in Europe, Hassan Kerde in Asia-Pacific, Charl Jonck in Africa and Fabio Luersen in the Americas.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16)[Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") defeated Andy Lavin, [Rodney Goggins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Goggins "Rodney Goggins"), Stuart Watson and Matthew Ford to win the Golden Ticket tournament to qualify for the final stages.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTBurden-17)

The winner of the event received £20,000, with the runner-up earning £10,000.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)

[![Image 7: photo of Dominic Dale](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a0/Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg/250px-Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dominic_Dale_PHC_2016-2.jpg)

[![Image 8: photo of Joe Perry](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/38/Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2013-01-31_01.jpg/250px-Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2013-01-31_01.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Joe_Perry_at_Snooker_German_Masters_(DerHexer)_2013-01-31_01.jpg)

The first round took place on 7 and 8 May, each match played as the best of 7 [frames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#frame "Glossary of cue sports terms").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[Joe Perry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Perry_(snooker_player) "Joe Perry (snooker player)") made two breaks of 76 to take a 2‍–‍0 lead against Fabio Luersen and also compiled a 94 and a 59 to win 4‍–‍2.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-18)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) "I was a little bit nervous which I was pleased about, I didn't want to be flat and not care," Perry said. [Craig Steadman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Steadman "Craig Steadman") recovered from 0‍–‍2 against [Dominic Dale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominic_Dale "Dominic Dale") to tie the scores, but Dale then won the fifth frame and compiled a [century break](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Century_break "Century break") of 107 in the sixth to clinch a 4‍–‍2 victory.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-20) "To win a tournament at the Crucible would be fantastic—it's a special place to play," Dale said. Wayne Townsend won the first frame of the match against the defending champion, [Igor Figueiredo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Figueiredo "Igor Figueiredo"), with a break of 53 and on the final [black ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#black_ball "Glossary of cue sports terms"). Figueiredo replied with a half-century of his own and then took the lead at 2‍–‍1. Townsend won three frames on the spin, the last one again on the final black, to seal victory.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-FigueiredoTownsend-21)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19) "I'm on cloud nine. I was playing the world champion and I've knocked him out! There's no reason why I can't be the world champion and there is nobody here I can't beat," Townsend said after the match.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19)[Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") manufactured breaks of 51, 89, 72 and 51 to defeat [Andrew Norman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Norman_(snooker_player) "Andrew Norman (snooker player)") 4‍–‍1.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-22) "If you enjoy it then the chances are that you will play better," Canavan conceded afterwards.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Townsendstuns-19)

[Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden") faced [Jimmy White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_White "Jimmy White"), winner of the event in [2010](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_World_Seniors_Championship "2010 World Seniors Championship"), [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_World_Seniors_Championship "2019 World Seniors Championship"), [2020](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_World_Seniors_Championship "2020 World Seniors Championship") and [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Seniors_Championship "2023 World Seniors Championship").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WSTlineup-16) Burden won the first two frames, but White produced a 82 break in the third to halve the deficit. Burden won the fourth frame on the [re-spotted black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#re-spotted_black "Glossary of cue sports terms") and manufactured a 92 break in the fifth to advance into the quarter-finals.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WhiteBurden-23)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) Burden commented after the match that he had first practiced with White when he was 15 years old and that he was sure White would want him to go on to win the tournament now: "We've had this amazing friendship for many years and I don't get any pleasure in beating Jimmy [White] but I was focused on winning and I had to blank out who I was playing."[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24)[Ken Doherty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Doherty "Ken Doherty") took a 2‍–‍0 lead against Charl Jonck, but Jonck went on to win four consecutive frames, featuring breaks of 64 and 63, to win the match.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-25)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) "That was surreal. It was the lifelong ambition becoming a reality," Jonck said.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24)[Tony Drago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Drago "Tony Drago") compiled a 75 break in the first frame of his duel with [Gerard Greene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerard_Greene "Gerard Greene"). The match went into a [decider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_cue_sports_terms#deciding_frame "Glossary of cue sports terms"), which Drago won aided by a break of 68.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-DragoGreene-26)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) Hassan Kerde [whitewashed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitewash_(sport) "Whitewash (sport)")[Tony Knowles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Knowles_(snooker_player) "Tony Knowles (snooker player)"), making breaks of 53, 62, 66 and 59 in the process.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-27)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24) "I'm over the moon. I've watched the Crucible for the last 20 years and to just come and watch a match would have been awesome," Kerde said afterwards.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-WDdowned-24)

The quarter-finals took place on 9 May, each match played as the best of 7 frames.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) Dale compiled breaks of 97, 99 and 128 as he beat Perry 4‍–‍1.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-28) "I've been practicing hard here and I've found some form. I was confident going into the match," Dale commented.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29) In his match against Burden, Drago won the first frame and then took two consecutive frames on the re-spotted black to edge 3‍–‍0 in front. Burden won four on the spin, featuring breaks of 53 and 51, to advance into the semi-finals.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-DragoBurden-30)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29)

Kerde and Jonck shared the first four frames, but Kerde then took two, one of them with a break of 85, to win the match.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-31) "I'm the first person to come from Australia and reach the semi-finals of the World Seniors Snooker Championship and hopefully I can do the country proud," Kerde said.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-quarters-29) Canavan took a 3‍–‍1 lead against Townsend, who compiled an 85 break in the fifth frame to halve the deficit. Canavan went on to take the following frame and seal victory with a 4‍–‍2 result.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-CanavanTownsend-32)

The semi-finals took place on 10 May, both matches played as the best of 11 frames.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2) Burden produced breaks of 57 and 65 as he took a 4‍–‍0 lead against Kerde. Kerde replied by winning two consecutive frames and halving the deficit, but Burden made a break of 97 to go 5‍–‍2 in front and won the following frame to clinch victory.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-BurdenKerde-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34) "It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final," Burden said afterwards.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-BurdenKerde-33)

Canavan and Dale shared the first four frames of their semi-final. Dale then made back-to-back century breaks, of 109 and 131, and won another frame to go within one of victory at 5‍–‍2. Canavan, however, won four consecutive frames, including the decider, to book a place in the final.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-CanavanDale-35)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34) "It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting," Canavan confessed.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-semis-34)

[![Image 9: Alfie Burden playing a shot](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0c/Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2015-02-05_01.jpg/250px-Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_%28DerHexer%29_2015-02-05_01.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alfie_Burden_and_Thorsten_M%C3%BCller_at_Snooker_German_Masters_(DerHexer)_2015-02-05_01.jpg)

[Alfie Burden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfie_Burden "Alfie Burden")_(pictured in 2015)_ defeated [Aaron Canavan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Canavan "Aaron Canavan") 8‍–‍4 in the final to claim his first [World Seniors Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Seniors_Championship "World Seniors Championship") title.

On 11 May, Burden and Canavan contested the best-of-15-frame final, which was divided into three mini-sessions of five frames each.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36) Both players were competing in a World Seniors final for the second time, Canavan having won the title in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_World_Seniors_Championship "2018 World Seniors Championship") and Burden having been runner-up in [2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_World_Seniors_Championship "2023 World Seniors Championship"). The first five-frame mini-session was refereed by [Michaela Tabb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michaela_Tabb "Michaela Tabb"), who retired from traditional snooker refereeing after the tournament, following a 24-year career that had included two [World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Snooker_Championship "World Snooker Championship") finals.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-37) Canavan won the opening frame, but Burden then won four consecutive frames with breaks including 74 and 54 as he moved 4–1 ahead.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36) Proletina Velichkova refereed the remainder of the final.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-38)

Canavan won the first frame of the second mini-session, but Burden took three consecutive frames with breaks of 65, 109, and 80. Canavan won the 8th frame to leave Burden leading 7–3. The third and final mini-session lasted two frames, as Canavan won frame 11 but Burden made a 76 break in the 12th to secure an 8–4 victory and win his first World Seniors title. He said afterwards: "I'm absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It's been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it's been well documented that I think I've underachieved in my career but you've got to enjoy this moment."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-Burden.Win-36)

Numbers in parentheses after the players' names are [seedings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seeding_(sports) "Seeding (sports)").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-wstorder-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-snookerorg2025-2)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-39)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_World_Seniors_Championship#cite_note-PIKEFINAL-40)

[Expanded Field for the 2026 World Seniors Championship](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/11/15/expanded-field-for-the-2026-world-seniors-championship/)
======================================================================================================================================================

[November 15, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/11/15/expanded-field-for-the-2026-world-seniors-championship/)[seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/)[Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

[This was shared on the WSS website](https://seniorssnooker.com/world-seniors-snooker-championship-expanded-for-2026/) a couple of days ago and it’s great news:

> World Seniors Snooker Championship Expanded for 2026
> ----------------------------------------------------
> 
> 
> **World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is pleased to announce that the 2026 World Seniors Snooker Championship will return to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield with an expanded field.**
> 
> 
> The flagship event, which will take place on 6-10 May 2026, will be shown live on Channel 5 in the UK and feature an increased line-up of 24 players with a two-table set up in the early rounds.
> 
> ![Image 4: A snooker tournament viewed from the audience perspective shows the setup of the table, lights, stage, and surrounding spectators](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image.png?w=1024)
> The 2015 Crucible champion Stuart Bingham will make his World Seniors Snooker Championship debut next May, as will former UK and Masters champion Matthew Stevens, 12-time World Women’s Snooker champion Reanne Evans and ranking event winner Anthony Hamilton.
> 
> 
> Jimmy White will be looking to win a record-extending fifth World Seniors Snooker Championship title while 1997 world champion Ken Doherty aims for Seniors glory at the Crucible for the first time.
> 
> ![Image 5: Snooker player aims with a cue, with red balls and a blue ball in the frame](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-1.png?w=1024)
> Defending champion Alfie Burden, Tony Drago, Joe Perry and Dominic Dale will also return to the sport’s most iconic venue in 2026 with six further players to be confirmed in due course.
> 
> 
> A global field once again sees each continental Seniors champion earning a place in the tournament. Brazil’s Igor Figueiredo, champion in 2024, will make his return after lifting the Pan-American Seniors Championship title earlier this year while there is also a second consecutive appearance for Craig Steadman after he retained the European title last month.
> 
> 
> Mohamed Samy Elkhayat, from Egypt, earns his place as the African Seniors champion and will be joined by the Asia-Pacific winner while four further places will be earned by qualifiers from the World Seniors Tour events.
> 
> ![Image 6: Trophy for a snooker event, placed on a pedestal with the Strachan Cloth logo on it, in an arena with blue lights](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/image-2.png?w=799)
> Jason Francis, Chairman of WSS, said: “_I am so pleased to announce our strongest ever field as we enter our new deal with Sheffield City Council, which will see the World Seniors Snooker Championship remain at the Crucible Theatre for at least the next two years_.”
> 
> 
> “_By expanding our event we can give more players the ultimate dream of playing competitive snooker at the sport’s most famous venue. We have six more players to invite and are working on some securing some legends to complete our field. The 2026 World Seniors Snooker Championships promises to be the biggest and best yet – another Sheffield snooker event for Sheffield people_.”

This promises to be interesting indeed, and fairer with more spots for qualifiers coming through the Seniors events tour.

Burden Lands World Seniors Crown
================================

12th May 2025
General

By World Snooker Tour

Share

[](mailto:?body=%0D%0A%0D%0A%0D%0AWorld%20Snooker%20Tour%20%20-%20%20Burden%20Lands%20World%20Seniors%20Crown%0D%0A%0D%0Ahttps://www.wst.tv/news/2025/may/12/burden-lands-world-seniors-crown/)

![Image 13: A 32x32 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://www.wst.tv/widgets/horizontal-line/colour-logo.svg)

**Alfie Burden won the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship, beating Aaron Canavan 8-4 in the final at the Crucible on Sunday.**

*   [Results](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/results)

The 48-year-old, who was the last player to qualify for the event via the Golden Ticket Play-Off last month, came through a strong field at the famous venue to lift the most prestigious title in seniors snooker for the first time.

![Image 14: Man standing in front of a crowd, holding up a trophy in celebration](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_2336-300x200.jpg)

Burden’s campaign began with a repeat of the 2023 World Seniors Snooker Championship final and he exacted revenge on four-time winner Jimmy White, before showing his fighting qualities from 3-0 down against Maltese legend Tony Drago to advance to the semi-finals.

A comfortable 6-2 victory over Australian debutant Hassan Kerde then set up a title match meeting with 2018 champion Aaron Canavan from Jersey after he stunned Dominic Dale in the last four.

![Image 15: Two men dressed in formal black attire stand on either side of a woman holding a trophy, positioned behind a snooker table with balls on it, and a crowd is visible in the background](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0003-300x200.jpg)

The best-of-15 frame final was split into three mini-sessions of five frames and the first of these saw a moment of history as Michaela Tabb, who became the first female referee to take charge of a World Snooker Championship final in 2009, took charge of her final frames at the Crucible Theatre.

It was Canavan who broke the deadlock but the Englishman quickly hit back to take four successive frames, with help from contributions of 74 and 54, to lead 4-1 at the first interval.

![Image 16: Snooker player aiming his shot on the pool table, while the referee oversees his play](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0086-300x200.jpg)

A 75 saw the cueist from Jersey reduce the deficit before Burden once again showed off his scoring prowess by hit consecutive breaks 65, 109 and 80 to move one away from victory at 7-2.

Canavan was able to avoid defeat before the second interval as he took frame 10 and further threatened a comeback by taking the next to put the scoreline at 7-4.

Burden admitted afterwards that, even at 7-3 ahead, he had told his coach Patsy Fagan that he “wasn’t fancying winning” but there were few signs of nerves in the title-winning frame as he fired in a flamboyant break of 76 to get over the line as an 8-4 victor.

Following the victory, Burden said: “I’m absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It’s been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it’s been well documented that I think I’ve underachieved in my career but you’ve got to enjoy this moment.

“It was a strong field this week and I felt like I played the best snooker and deserved to win the tournament. Jimmy White texted me this morning and so did Ken Doherty – we are all great friends and players get behind each other. Only one person can win and this was my week.”

World Seniors Snooker Championship to remain at the Crucible until at least 2027
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

World Seniors Snooker, Sheffield City Council and Sheffield Theatres are delighted to announce a new deal, which will see the World Seniors Snooker Championship remain at the Crucible Theatre until at least 2027.

 Share this story 

The World Seniors Snooker Championship, which was broadcast live last year on Channel 5, follows on from the World Snooker Championship and gives snooker legends including Jimmy White, Ken Doherty, Tony Drago and more another chance to play at snooker’s most famous venue which defined many of their careers.

The 2025 Championship in May will see players from eight countries compete for the title won last year by Igor Figueiredo from Brazil. It will also see the first collaboration with Sheffield Hallam University’s sports business management students, who will be given the opportunity to work on a major TV Snooker broadcast.

> “Fantastic news! The Crucible has been the home of snooker and the World Seniors gives me and others who have given their life to the sport a chance to play their again for a World title.”
> 
> 
> Jimmy White, Four-time World Seniors Snooker champion and World Snooker Champ

> “It’s great news to confirm our Championship will be staying in Sheffield at the Crucible.
> 
> 
> "Our strategic partnership with the Council allows the World Seniors Snooker to showcase everything that is great about Sheffield.
> 
> 
> "This year as well as repeating our Seniors of Sheffield Day we are running a Business and Youth of Sheffield Day alongside our work with Sheffield Hallam University.”
> 
> 
> Jason Francis, Chairman of World Seniors Snooker

> “Sheffield loves snooker, which is why we are delighted to announce that the city will continue to host the World Seniors Snooker Championship for at least two more years, at the world-renowned Crucible Theatre. t
> 
> 
> “This year’s event is set to be bigger than ever before, with the all-new Sheffield Youth and Business Days, alongside the Sheffield Seniors Day that has been a huge success in previous years. We can’t wait to welcome the Championship back to the city this year and to support them in growing the tournament here in Sheffield, in the coming years.”
> 
> 
> Councillor Tom Hunt, Leader of Sheffield City Council

> “We are delighted to continue to host the World Seniors Snooker Championship at the Crucible. As the tournament expands, with Seniors of Sheffield, Business and Youth Day, it is wonderful to welcome even more people to this exceptional theatre.”
> 
> 
> Bookey Oshin, Deputy CEO Sheffield Theatres

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will be played from Wednesday 7 May to Sunday 11 May 2025.

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship –Semi-Finals
========================================================

[May 11, 2025 May 11, 2025](https://seniorsnooker.com/2025/05/11/the-2025-world-seniors-snooker-championship-sfs/)[seniorsnooker](https://seniorsnooker.com/author/seniorsnooker/)[Uncategorized](https://seniorsnooker.com/category/uncategorized/)

Today’s final at the Crucible will be competed between two players who have been here before: Aaron Canavan, who won the title in 2018, and Alfie Burden who was runner-up in 2023.

[Here is how the semi-finals unfolded as reported by WSS](https://seniorssnooker.com/burden-and-canavan-set-up-world-final-meeting/):

> **Burden and Canavan Set Up World Final Meeting**
> -------------------------------------------------
> 
> 
> **Alfie Burden and Aaron Canavan will meet in the final of the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship on Sunday afternoon.**
> 
> 
> The two former finalists reached the title match by overcoming Hassan Kerde and Dominic Dale respectively on a memorable semi-final Saturday at the iconic Crucible Theatre.
> 
> ![Image 7: Player taking a shot in a snooker match, refereed by a woman in a dark suit and white gloves](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image.png?w=1024)
> Canavan heads into the title match aiming to become only the second multiple champion of the most prestigious event in seniors snooker, after four-time winner Jimmy White, while Burden hopes to go one step further than he did in 2023 when he ended as runner-up to ‘The Whirlwind’.
> 
> 
> Former professional Burden and Asia-Pacific Seniors champion Kerde, from Australia, kicked off a bumper session with a best-of-11 frame contest.
> 
> ![Image 8: Snooker player strikes a ball on a snooker table as the referee and audience watch in the background](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-1.png?w=1024)
> Burden was in fine form and he wasted no time in racing into a 4-0 lead with breaks of 57 and 65. The Australian briefly rallied, taking back-to-back frames to half the deficit, but a rapid-fire contribution of 97 put Burden back in the acendency and he secured his place in the final by taking the next frame.
> 
> 
> Post-match, Burden said: “It was a tough game but I was pleased with the way I played and it stands me in good stead for the final. I’ve prepared well, practiced hard and I feel confident. I feel really strong – I’m going out and expecting to win tomorrow.”
> 
> ![Image 9: Two mature male snooker players stand in front of a 'World Seniors Champions' backdrop, one holding a cue case and the other a snooker cue](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-2.png?w=1024)
> The second semi-final of the afternoon saw Canavan face Dale and, after sharing the first four frames of the contest, ‘The Spaceman’ appeared to step up a gear and fired in back-to-back century breaks of 109 and 131 before moving one frame from victory by taking the seventh.
> 
> 
> The man from Jersey refused to go away, however, and managed to take the next three frames with a top visit of 65 to force an unlikely deciding frame.
> 
> ![Image 10: A focused snooker player in a black jersey is captured lining up a shot with his cue, with a concentrated expression, with a crowd of spectators watches from the background](https://seniorsnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/image-3.png?w=1024)
> The decider was a nervy affair with both players spurning golden opportunities for the win. Ultimately, it was Canavan who took it on the colours to complete a famous comeback and set up a final meeting with Burden.
> 
> 
> Canavan said: “It was tough. After last night, I was really tired but I gave myself a good talking to in the dressing room and came out fighting. It’s dream, you never think that you will get there and then all of a sudden something happens and you’re actually living the dream.”

### 5 renews World Seniors Snooker Championship deal

April 10, 2025

![Image 8: A player's hand with cue stick aligned above a snooker table](https://www.advanced-television.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/snooker-1024x576.jpg)

[![Image 9: A 468x59 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://atv-adsrv.com/images/bb8af4cca3fa25f712ddd35eb49dac28.gif)](https://atv-adsrv.com/ads/www/delivery/cl.php?bannerid=784&zoneid=17&source=%7Bobfs%3A%7D&sig=f2478824587fdb08d14d76dd01495fe1886577dc754ed31bc988b3ab11115e35&oadest=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.promptlink.com%2Fproducts%2Fcpm.html)

![Image 10: A 1x1 image, likely be a tacker probe](https://atv-adsrv.com/ads/www/delivery/lg.php?bannerid=784&campaignid=736&zoneid=17&source={obfs:}&loc=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.advanced-television.com%2F2025%2F04%2F10%2F5-renews-world-seniors-snooker-championship-deal%2F&cb=f894edcfa2)

5 has secured the exclusive broadcast rights for the World Seniors Snooker Championship for the second year in a row. Set to take place from May 7th to 11th, the deal will see all the action from Sheffield’s Crucible Theatre broadcast live on 5 and its digital channel 5Action, enabling a wide audience access to all the excitement of Seniors snooker.

Produced by independent production company Sunset+Vine the rights package includes live coverage of the tournament, with daytime and weekend sessions. Pundits and commentators will provide ongoing insight and opinions on the tournament, the performances of players, and all the key moments from the Championship.

[![Image 11: A 468x60 small image, likely a logo, icon or avatar](https://atv-adsrv.com/images/786447837c09e235dd4cea723e80acab.jpg)](https://atv-adsrv.com/ads/www/delivery/cl.php?bannerid=782&zoneid=18&source=%7Bobfs%3A%7D&sig=0e857d4e048f19e52e54e931f4498105950d4f58eccc47e63c7c00c4b3ce6b1d&oadest=https%3A%2F%2Fadvanced-television.tv%2Findex.php%2Fchannel%2F44%2Finnovation-ibc-2025%2F%23)

![Image 12: A 1x1 image, likely be a tacker probe](https://atv-adsrv.com/ads/www/delivery/lg.php?bannerid=782&campaignid=734&zoneid=18&source={obfs:}&loc=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.advanced-television.com%2F2025%2F04%2F10%2F5-renews-world-seniors-snooker-championship-deal%2F&cb=4c52fd1713)

“The World Seniors Snooker Championship is celebrated for showcasing the extraordinary talents of legendary players competing at the highest level, so we’re excited to broadcast this much-loved event on 5, providing it with the platform and scale it deserves,” commented Ben Frow, 5’s Chief Content Officer. “Not only will we enhance the experience for snooker enthusiasts and sports lovers alike, we will also bring in a wider audience than would otherwise have access to the event. This deal underscores our ambition to establish 5 as a destination for our viewers to enjoy sports content – watch this space.”

Jason Francis, Chairman of World Seniors Snooker, said: “Its brilliant to be back and bring Snooker once again to a free-to-air audience. This is our 6th event on 5 in under 18 months and it’s been so well received”

Titus Hill – Executive Producer, Sunset+Vine, added: “At Sunset+Vine we have grown up with the legends of the sport like Jimmy White and Ken Doherty and the chance to produce the programming for 5 on the World Seniors Championship will be a career highlight for many of our team. Our production at The Crucible will feature other stars of the sport including Dennis Taylor, Cliff Thorburn and John Virgo.”

JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025 – How To Follow
===================================================================

9th May 2025

[Home](https://wpbsa.com/) » JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship 2025 – How To Follow

**Snooker returns to the Crucible Theatre on 7-11 May 2025 as the JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship takes place at the sport’s most iconic venue.**

*   [Draw](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/knockout)
*   [Schedule](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/schedule)

*   [Player List](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/players)

Igor Figueiredo is the defending champion in an international field of 16 players from nine nations including Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and more.

The Championship can be watched live on Channel 5 and 5Action in the UK and you can also follow the event via [WPBSA SnookerScores](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025).

World Seniors Snooker to be Shown Live on 5
===========================================

28th July 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » World Seniors Snooker to be Shown Live on 5

**World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is delighted to announce that both the 2025 British Seniors Open and 2026 World Seniors Snooker Championship will be broadcast live on 5.**

The British Seniors Open will return snooker to Derby for the first time in 32 years and feature star names like Jimmy White, Ken Doherty and Matthew Stevens.

![Image 6: A large crowd gathered for a snooker tournament where presenters are interviewing the participants in front of a snooker table](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/FouldsEvansRichardsonCasey-300x200.jpg)

Coverage will begin at 13:00 on Boxing day with the first of two quarter finals, a further session with two more quarter finals will be played from 19:00.

Both Semi Finals will take place from 13:00 on Saturday 27 December with the final starting at the same time on the Sunday.

This new deal also confirms the continuation of the World Seniors Snooker Championship from the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield on 5 in May 2026.

![Image 7: A wide angle view of a snooker match in progress](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_9833-300x200.jpg)

World Seniors Snooker Chairman Jason Francis said “Our partnership with 5 has brought top class snooker to millions of fans in the UK and Ireland since 2023. Being able to stage a new event with them this Christmas is really exciting and it’s great for fans to know the World Seniors Snooker Championship will be back on the channel in May”

Raphael Pendergast, Acting Head of Sport at 5 said “We’re pleased to extend our relationship with World Seniors Snooker, and bring the strongest ever line-ups of Snooker legends into viewers’ homes at Christmas”.
